block.prompt:
SPEAKING — in pairs or threes.

For each of the four situations below, discuss: would CASH or a CARD / PHONE be better here, and WHY? Use at least one „weighing options“ phrase from the language box (On the one hand… / The main drawback is…). Be ready to report your group's view to the class.

1. Buying second-hand furniture from a stranger at a flea market.
2. Giving a nine-year-old child their weekly pocket money.
3. A day when the electricity and the internet are down across the whole town.
4. Paying for a song or an app online.

payload.stem: For each situation, agree on the better payment method AND a reason. It is fine if you and your partner disagree — say so, and defend your choice.

block.answer_key: There is no fixed key — each choice can be defended. Typical reasoning: (1) Cash — private, no fee for the seller, and a stranger may not accept cards; card — no risk of carrying a lot of money. (2) Cash — a child learns the value of money when they can see and hold it; card/app — parents can track spending. (3) Cash — the only thing that still works when systems are down (a strong argument for keeping cash); card — useless without power/internet. (4) Card/app — you cannot post coins to an online shop; the whole transaction is digital. Reward answers that WEIGH a trade-off rather than just naming a method.
block.acceptable_reasoning: Für jedes Szenario sind beide Antworten vertretbar; entscheidend ist die Qualität der Begründung und das Abwägen (Vor-/Nachteil). Szenario 3 ist bewusst so gebaut, dass es ein starkes Bargeld-Argument liefert (Ausfallsicherheit) — das darf, muss aber nicht erkannt werden.
watch_outs: Häufig wird nur die Methode genannt (‚card') ohne Begründung. Die Rückfrage ‚why?' konsequent einfordern.
Szenario 3 (Stromausfall) ist der Denkanstoß für die spätere Debatte — nicht vorwegnehmen, aber im Kopf behalten.
Redemittel-Kasten aktiv nutzen lassen: ‚the main drawback is…' statt bloßem ‚because it's better'.

subject: Lebende Fremdsprache
kompetenzbereich: An Gesprächen teilnehmen und zusammenhängendes Sprechen
